```{r}
save_figure(
  fig_forest("P3", "P3: two references per class help, least on microstructure",
             "Two references per class (k = 2) minus none (k = 0), both with the final description (pans: generic)."),
  "F5_paired_P3", height = forest_heights, paper_height = forest_paper_heights
)
```

## Table of the comparisons

```{r}
#| label: paired-marks
# The mark of each comparison: the mark of a side whose Platt fit reverses
# the raw order or is not defined. The sides come from the plan of
# R/fair_evaluate.R; the CLIP baseline of P1 has one k per dataset.
plan <- c("jev", "clef") |>
  purrr::map(\(m) dplyr::mutate(fair$comparison_plan(m, dataset_order), model = m)) |>
  purrr::list_rbind()
side_a <- plan |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::filter(slopes, k == k_main),
                    by = c("model", final = "description", "dataset"))
side_b <- plan |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::rename(slopes, b_model = model, b_desc = description),
                    by = c("b_model", "b_desc", "dataset"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  dplyr::filter(is.na(b_k) | k == b_k)
comparison_flags <- dplyr::bind_rows(side_a, side_b) |>
  dplyr::summarise(flag = stringr::str_c(unique(slope_mark(platt_slope)), collapse = ""),
                   .by = c(comparison, model, dataset))
# The meaning of the marks, for the caption of the table.
paired_marks <- ""
if (any(comparison_flags$flag != "")) {
  paired_marks <- stringr::str_c(" A mark on a comparison applies to one of its two sides.",
                                 mark_caption(comparison_flags$flag))
}
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-paired
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'stringr::str_c("Paired comparisons on the test sets: difference (95% paired bootstrap interval) for balanced accuracy, MCC and AUC, and the exact McNemar p-value, before and after the Holm adjustment within each model.", paired_marks)'
#| eval: !expr has_paired
#| include: !expr has_paired
# Table T6: one row per comparison, model and dataset.
t6 <- paired |>
  dplyr::left_join(comparison_flags, by = c("comparison", "model", "dataset")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(cell = stringr::str_glue("{signed(difference, 3)} ({fmt(low, 3)} to {fmt(high, 3)})")) |>
  dplyr::select(comparison, flag, model, dataset, metric, cell, mcnemar_p, holm_p,
                holm_family_size) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = cell) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(dataset, dataset_order), comparison,
                 match(model, names(model_labels))) |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset],
    Comparison = stringr::str_c(comparison, dplyr::coalesce(flag, "")),
    Model = model_labels[model],
    `Balanced accuracy` = as.character(bal_accuracy), MCC = as.character(mcc),
    AUC = as.character(roc_auc),
    `McNemar p` = fmt_p(mcnemar_p), `Holm p` = fmt_p(holm_p),
    `Holm tests` = holm_family_size
  )
save_table(t6, "T6_paired_comparisons",
           stringr::str_c("Paired comparisons on the test sets.", paired_marks),
           digits = 3, page_length = 30, group = "Dataset")
```

# Reference curve

@fig-reference-curve shows the test balanced accuracy and AUC against the number of references per class, k = 0, 1, 2 and 4. The decision models use the final description (pans: generic) at every k, so only the references change. For CLIP, k = 0 is zero-shot, and k > 0 uses the same references as the decision models. All values use Platt scaling on C. The bars give the paired 95% interval of the change from k = 0, placed at the value: a bar that does not reach the value at k = 0 shows a change that the test images support. A bar stops at 0 and 1, the limits of both metrics.

```{r}
#| label: curve-numbers
# Numbers for the text below: the balanced accuracy of one model at one k,
# and the change from k = 2 to k = 4.
curve_ba <- function(m, ds, kk) {
  k_curve$value[k_curve$model == m & k_curve$dataset == ds & k_curve$k == kk &
                  k_curve$metric == "bal_accuracy"]
}
change_2_to_4 <- k_curve |>
  dplyr::filter(metric == "bal_accuracy", k %in% c(2, 4)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(change = value[k == 4] - value[k == 2], .by = c(model, dataset))
max_change <- function(m, datasets = dataset_order) {
  fmt(max(abs(change_2_to_4$change[change_2_to_4$model == m &
                                     change_2_to_4$dataset %in% datasets])), 3)
}
# The k = 0 points whose Platt fit has a negative slope (decision D82): the
# decision models with the description of the curve, and CLIP zero-shot.
reversed_k0 <- k_curve |>
  dplyr::filter(k == 0, metric == "bal_accuracy") |>
  dplyr::mutate(description = dplyr::case_when(model == "clip" ~ "zero",
                                               dataset == "pan_images" ~ "generic",
                                               .default = "final")) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(slopes, by = c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")) |>
  dplyr::filter(platt_slope < 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(model, names(model_labels)), match(dataset, dataset_order)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = stringr::str_c(
    dplyr::if_else(model == "clip", "CLIP zero-shot", model_labels[model]), " on ",
    stringr::str_to_lower(dataset_labels[dataset])
  ))
reversed_k0_text <- as.character(knitr::combine_words(reversed_k0$label, oxford_comma = FALSE))
reversed_k0_caption <- ""
if (nrow(reversed_k0) > 0) {
  reversed_k0_caption <- stringr::str_c(
    " At k = 0, the Platt fit has a negative slope and reverses the raw scores ",
    "(decision D82) for ", reversed_k0_text, "."
  )
}
```

The decision models get most of their gain from the first references. From k = 2 to k = 4, the balanced accuracy of JEV changes by `r max_change("jev")` or less; the largest change is on microstructure, from `r fmt(curve_ba("jev", "microstructure", 2), 3)` to `r fmt(curve_ba("jev", "microstructure", 4), 3)`. On extrusion, textiles, pipe staple and pans, most of the JEV gain comes at k = 1: from k = 0 to k = 1, JEV gains `r fmt(curve_ba("jev", "pipe_staple", 1) - curve_ba("jev", "pipe_staple", 0), 3)` on pipe staple and `r fmt(curve_ba("jev", "pan_images", 1) - curve_ba("jev", "pan_images", 0), 3)` on pans. From k = 2 to k = 4, Clef-Flash changes by `r max_change("clef", setdiff(dataset_order, "pan_images"))` or less, except on pans, where it drops from `r fmt(curve_ba("clef", "pan_images", 2), 3)` to `r fmt(curve_ba("clef", "pan_images", 4), 3)`. CLIP with the same references gains more slowly: on textiles, it has `r fmt(curve_ba("clip", "textiles", 2), 3)` at k = 2 and `r fmt(curve_ba("clip", "textiles", 4), 3)` at k = 4. At k = 0, the Platt fit reverses the raw scores (negative slope; decision D82) for `r reversed_k0_text`.

```{r}
#| label: curve-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_decision, "Without them, the figure shows CLIP only.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-reference-curve
#| fig-cap: !expr 'stringr::str_c("Test balanced accuracy and AUC against the number of references per class (Platt scaling on C). Bars: paired 95% interval of the change from k = 0, placed at the value and cut at the limits of the metric (0 and 1).", reversed_k0_caption)'
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 3.8
# Values and intervals; the interval of the change from k = 0 is moved to the
# value at k (value at k = 0 plus the bounds) and cut at 0 and 1, the limits
# of balanced accuracy and AUC. Models side by side at each k.
curve <- k_curve |>
  dplyr::filter(metric %in% c("bal_accuracy", "roc_auc")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(k0 = value[k == 0], .by = c(model, dataset, metric)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    low_value = pmax(k0 + low, 0), high_value = pmin(k0 + high, 1),
    x = k + unname(c(jev = -0.12, clef = 0, clip = 0.12)[model]),
    model = factor(model_labels[model], names(model_colors)),
    metric = factor(metric_labels[metric], metric_labels[c("bal_accuracy", "roc_auc")]),
    dataset = label_dataset(dataset)
  )
curve_models <- intersect(names(model_colors), as.character(curve$model))

# Figure F6: metrics by dataset (two-column) or datasets by metric
# (one-column).
fig_curve <- function(layout, paper = FALSE) {
  d <- curve
  if (paper) {
    levels(d$metric)[levels(d$metric) == metric_labels[["bal_accuracy"]]] <- "Accuracy"
  }
  if (layout == "one-column") {
    levels(d$dataset) <- short_labels[dataset_order]
    facets <- ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = ggplot2::vars(dataset), cols = ggplot2::vars(metric))
  } else {
    facets <- ggplot2::facet_grid(rows = ggplot2::vars(metric), cols = ggplot2::vars(dataset))
  }
  model_text <- purrr::map_chr(curve_models, \(m) paint(m, model_colors[[m]]))
  ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(x, value, colour = model)) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.5) +
    ggplot2::geom_linerange(ggplot2::aes(ymin = low_value, ymax = high_value),
                            linewidth = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = model_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 1, 2, 4)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0.4, 1, 0.2)) +
    ggplot2::coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.3, 1.02)) +
    facets +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = headline("Beyond two references, the decision models gain little", layout),
      subtitle = subline(
        layout,
        "Test results of ", stringr::str_c(model_text, collapse = ", "),
        " by references per class (k), after Platt scaling ",
        "on the calibration set C. CLIP at k = 0 is zero-shot. Bars: paired ",
        "95% interval of the change from k = 0, placed at the value and cut at 0 and 1."
      ),
      x = "References per class (k)", y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_paper(layout)
}
save_figure(fig_curve, "F6_reference_curve",
            height = c("one-column" = 6.4, "two-column" = 3.8))
```

# Calibration

Raw scores are not probabilities that a quality engineer can trust. @tbl-calibration gives the ECE, the Brier score and the log loss on the test set before (raw) and after Platt scaling on C. @fig-reliability shows the reliability diagrams of the decision models and of the CLIP baseline. The raw CLIP scores are the softmax of two cosine similarities, which differ little, so they stay near 0.5.

```{r}
#| label: calibration-numbers
# Raw and Platt metrics of the main methods.
calibration_rows <- c("raw", "platt") |>
  purrr::map(\(cal) dplyr::mutate(test_metrics(cal), calibration = cal)) |>
  purrr::list_rbind() |>
  dplyr::inner_join(main_configs, by = c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")) |>
  dplyr::select(method, flag, dataset, calibration, ece, brier_class, mn_log_loss) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = calibration,
                     values_from = c(ece, brier_class, mn_log_loss)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(dataset, dataset_order), match(method, main_methods$method))

# Numbers for the text below: the test ECE of the two decision models and
# the CLIP baseline, the methods of the reliability diagrams.
reliability_methods <- c("JEV, k = 2", "Clef-Flash, k = 2", "CLIP baseline")
ece_rows <- calibration_rows |>
  dplyr::filter(method %in% reliability_methods) |>
  dplyr::mutate(drop = ece_raw - ece_platt)
ece_of <- function(meth, ds, cal) {
  fmt(ece_rows[[stringr::str_c("ece_", cal)]][ece_rows$method == meth & ece_rows$dataset == ds], 3)
}
pan_ece <- ece_rows$ece_platt[ece_rows$dataset == "pan_images"]
other_ece <- ece_rows$ece_platt[ece_rows$dataset != "pan_images"]
```

Platt scaling lowers the test ECE most where the raw scores are far from calibrated. The largest drop is that of the CLIP baseline on textiles, from `r ece_of("CLIP baseline", "textiles", "raw")` to `r ece_of("CLIP baseline", "textiles", "platt")`. Outside pans, the ECE after Platt is `r fmt(min(other_ece), 3)` to `r fmt(max(other_ece), 3)` for the two decision models and the CLIP baseline. Platt does not lower the ECE everywhere: it raises it in `r sum(ece_rows$drop < 0)` of the `r nrow(ece_rows)` cases, for both decision models on extrusion and pans, and for the CLIP baseline on pipe staple. Pans have the highest ECE after Platt, `r fmt(min(pan_ece), 3)` to `r fmt(max(pan_ece), 3)`. The test ECE uses 10 equal bins, so with `r sum(test_set$dataset == "pan_images")` pan images it is noisy.

```{r}
#| label: calibration-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_decision, "Without them, the table and the figure show CLIP only.")
```

```{r}

#| tbl-cap: !expr 'stringr::str_c("Calibration on the test sets: ECE, Brier score and log loss of the raw scores and after Platt scaling on C.", mark_caption(calibration_rows$flag))'
# Table T7.
t7 <- calibration_rows |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset], Method = stringr::str_c(method, flag),
    `ECE raw` = ece_raw, `ECE Platt` = ece_platt,
    `Brier raw` = brier_class_raw, `Brier Platt` = brier_class_platt,
    `Log loss raw` = mn_log_loss_raw, `Log loss Platt` = mn_log_loss_platt
  )
save_table(t7, "T7_calibration",
           stringr::str_c("Calibration on the test sets.", mark_caption(calibration_rows$flag)),
           digits = 3, page_length = 25, group = "Dataset")

# The reliability figure below has one panel per method and dataset, for
# the two decision models and the CLIP baseline (reliability_methods). Its
# height follows the number of panels (five per row; three in the
# one-column size).
n_panels <- sum(calibration_rows$method %in% reliability_methods)
reliability_heights <- c(
  "one-column" = 1.5 + 1.5 * ceiling(n_panels / 3),
  "two-column" = 1.2 + 1.75 * ceiling(n_panels / 5)
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-reliability
#| fig-cap: "Reliability diagrams on the test sets: observed defect rate against the mean probability in 10 equal bins, for the raw scores and after Platt scaling on C."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: !expr reliability_heights[["two-column"]]
# Calibrated probabilities of every image, from the score files (the same
# fits as scripts/fair_evaluate.R).
calibrated <- list.files(scores_dir, pattern = "^(jev|clef|clip)_.+_(calibration|test)\\.csv$",
                         full.names = TRUE) |>
  purrr::map(read_csv_quiet) |>
  purrr::list_rbind() |>
  fair$calibrate_all()

# Test probabilities of the two decision models and the CLIP baseline, in
# 10 equal bins.
reliability <- main_configs |>
  dplyr::filter(method %in% reliability_methods) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::filter(calibrated, split == "test"),
                    by = c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(raw, platt), names_to = "calibration", values_to = "p") |>
  dplyr::mutate(bin = cut(p, seq(0, 1, 0.1), include.lowest = TRUE),
                y = as.integer(actual_class == "defective")) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean_p = mean(p), observed = mean(y), n = dplyr::n(),
                   .by = c(method, dataset, calibration, bin)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(method, dataset, calibration, mean_p) |>
  dplyr::mutate(calibration = factor(dplyr::if_else(calibration == "platt", "Platt", "raw"),
                                     names(calibration_colors)))

# Strip of each panel: dataset, method, and the test ECE before and after
# Platt in their colors. Panels go by method, then by dataset.
strip_text <- function(layout) {
  labels <- if (layout == "one-column") {
    stringr::str_replace(short_labels, "\n", "<br>")
  } else {
    dataset_labels
  }
  calibration_rows |>
    dplyr::filter(method %in% reliability_methods) |>
    dplyr::arrange(match(method, reliability_methods), match(dataset, dataset_order)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      method, dataset,
      strip = stringr::str_c(
        "**", labels[dataset], "**<br>", method, "<br>ECE ",
        paint(fmt(ece_raw), calibration_colors[["raw"]]), " to ",
        paint(fmt(ece_platt), calibration_colors[["Platt"]])
      ),
      strip = factor(strip, strip)
    )
}

# Figure F7: five panels per row (two-column) or three (one-column).
fig_reliability <- function(layout, paper = FALSE) {
  d <- dplyr::inner_join(reliability, strip_text(layout), by = c("method", "dataset"))
  ggplot2::ggplot(d, ggplot2::aes(mean_p, observed, colour = calibration)) +
    ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.3) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.55) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 0.9) +
    ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = calibration_colors) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
    ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(strip), ncol = if (layout == "one-column") 3 else 5) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = headline("Platt scaling fixes the worst raw scores, except on pans", layout),
      subtitle = subline(
        layout,
        paint("Raw", calibration_colors[["raw"]]), " scores and ",
        paint("Platt", calibration_colors[["Platt"]]),
        " probabilities on the test images (Platt fitted on the calibration ",
        "set C). Calibrated curves follow the diagonal. Strips give the test ",
        "ECE before and after Platt scaling."
      ),
      x = "Mean predicted defect probability (10 bins)",
      y = "Observed defect rate"
    ) +
    theme_paper(layout) +
    ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggtext::element_markdown(face = "plain", lineheight = 1.2))
}
save_figure(fig_reliability, "F7_reliability", height = reliability_heights)
```

# Time and cost {#sec-time}

This section gives the time that each method needs for one image, the total time of each step, and the calls, tokens and estimated cost of JEV. `scripts/fair_evaluate.R` makes `results/fair/summary/timing.csv` from the `elapsed_ms` column of the score files, from `clip_timing.csv` and `runs.csv` in `results/fair/timing/`, and from the TypeSafe call log. @sec-time-methods tells how each time is measured.

```{r}
#| label: time-data
# The timing summary, and the hardware of each method from runs.csv.
timing <- read_csv_quiet(
  file.path(summary_dir, "timing.csv"),
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = "d", model = "c", description = "c",
                          dataset = "c", split = "c")
)
runs_file <- file.path(results_root, "timing", "runs.csv")
hardware <- if (file.exists(runs_file)) {
  read_csv_quiet(runs_file, col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c")) |>
    dplyr::distinct(model, hardware)
} else {
  tibble::tibble(model = character(), hardware = character())
}
has_decision_time <- any(timing$model %in% c("jev", "clef") & !is.na(timing$median_ms))
has_clip_time <- any(timing$model == "clip" & !is.na(timing$median_ms))
has_cost <- any(!is.na(timing$n_calls))

# Median time of the CLIP baseline: pans against the other datasets.
clip_base <- dplyr::filter(timing, model == "clip", description == "baseline", split == "test")
clip_pan_ms <- clip_base$median_ms[clip_base$dataset == "pan_images"]
clip_other_ms <- mean(clip_base$median_ms[clip_base$dataset != "pan_images"])
if (length(clip_pan_ms) == 0) clip_pan_ms <- clip_other_ms <- NA_real_

# Median time of the decision models at k = 2 (final description; pans:
# generic): the range over the other datasets, and pans.
decision_ms <- dplyr::filter(timing, model %in% c("jev", "clef"), split == "test", k == k_main,
                             description == dplyr::if_else(dataset == "pan_images",
                                                           "generic", "final"))
ms_range <- function(m) {
  ms <- decision_ms$median_ms[decision_ms$model == m & decision_ms$dataset != "pan_images"]
  stringr::str_c(fmt(min(ms), 0), " to ", fmt(max(ms), 0))
}
ms_pan <- \(m) fmt(decision_ms$median_ms[decision_ms$model == m & decision_ms$dataset == "pan_images"], 0)

# Calls and estimated cost of JEV: the test runs, and all runs with a cost.
jev_calls <- dplyr::filter(timing, !is.na(n_calls))
jev_test_calls <- dplyr::filter(jev_calls, split == "test")
no_cost <- sum(is.na(jev_calls$cost_usd))
cost_note <- ""
if (no_cost > 0) {
  cost_note <- stringr::str_c(" The call log has no cost for ", no_cost,
                              " configurations; the total does not include them.")
}
# The cost sentence of the section JEV cost, only when the log has a cost.
cost_text <- ""
if (has_cost) {
  cost_text <- stringr::str_c(
    "The ", fmt(sum(jev_test_calls$n_calls), 0), " JEV calls of the test runs cost about USD ",
    fmt(sum(jev_test_calls$cost_usd, na.rm = TRUE)), ". All ", fmt(sum(jev_calls$n_calls), 0),
    " JEV calls of the description loops, the calibration runs and the test runs cost ",
    "about USD ", fmt(sum(jev_calls$cost_usd, na.rm = TRUE)), " (@tbl-cost)."
  )
}

# One sentence that names the hardware of each method.
hardware_text <- hardware |>
  dplyr::mutate(label = model_labels[model]) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(model, names(model_labels))) |>
  dplyr::summarise(text = stringr::str_c(label[1], ": ", stringr::str_c(hardware, collapse = ", ")),
                   .by = model) |>
  dplyr::pull(text) |>
  stringr::str_c(collapse = "; ")
```

The times come from different hardware: `r hardware_text`. JEV time includes the network and the queue of the service, and CLIP time does not. The methods are therefore not ranked on time alone.

## Time per image

@tbl-time gives the median and the interquartile range (Q1 to Q3) of the time per image on the test set. The CLIP time is the time of the timing pass, after one warm-up call. At k = 2, JEV needs a median of `r ms_range("jev")` ms per image on the four datasets other than pans, and `r ms_pan("jev")` ms on pans. Clef-Flash needs `r ms_range("clef")` ms, and `r ms_pan("clef")` ms on pans. The CLIP baseline needs a median of `r fmt(clip_pan_ms, 0)` ms for a pan image and `r fmt(clip_other_ms, 0)` ms on average for an image of the other datasets.

```{r}
#| label: time-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_decision_time, "Without them, the table shows CLIP only.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-time
#| tbl-cap: "Time per image on the test sets (ms): median and quartiles. JEV and Clef-Flash: the wall time of the call with the image preparation. CLIP: image loading, preparation, encoding and scoring on the local GPU, after one warm-up call. The hardware differs between the methods (see the text)."
#| eval: !expr has_clip_time || has_decision_time
#| include: !expr has_clip_time || has_decision_time
# Test rows of the main methods, with their hardware.
time_rows <- main_configs |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::filter(timing, split == "test", !is.na(median_ms)),
                    by = c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")) |>
  dplyr::left_join(hardware, by = "model") |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(dataset, dataset_order), match(method, main_methods$method))

# Table T8.
t8 <- time_rows |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset], Method = method, Hardware = hardware,
    Images = n_images, Median = median_ms, Q1 = q25_ms, Q3 = q75_ms
  )
save_table(t8, "T8_time_per_image", "Time per image on the test sets (ms).",
           digits = 1, page_length = 25, group = "Dataset")
```

## Total time

@tbl-total-time gives the total time of each step: the description loops (design images), the calibration runs and the test runs, summed over the configurations of a model and a dataset. The step of CLIP is the timing pass on the test images. The original scoring runs of CLIP were not timed.

```{r}
#| label: total-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_decision_time, "Without them, the table shows CLIP only.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-total-time
#| tbl-cap: "Total time of each step (seconds), summed over the configurations of a method and a dataset. Design: all candidates of the description loop. CLIP: the timing pass on the test images."
#| eval: !expr any(!is.na(timing$total_seconds))
#| include: !expr any(!is.na(timing$total_seconds))
step_labels <- c(design = "Design loop", calibration = "Calibration runs", test = "Test runs")
total_rows <- timing |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(total_seconds)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(runs = dplyr::n(), images = sum(n_images, na.rm = TRUE),
                   seconds = sum(total_seconds),
                   .by = c(model, dataset, split)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(dataset, dataset_order), match(model, names(model_labels)),
                 match(split, names(step_labels)))

# Table T9.
t9 <- total_rows |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset], Method = model_labels[model],
    Step = dplyr::if_else(model == "clip", "Timing pass", step_labels[split]),
    Configurations = runs, Images = images, `Total time (s)` = seconds
  )
save_table(t9, "T9_total_time", "Total time of each step (seconds).",
           digits = 1, page_length = 25, group = "Dataset")
```

## JEV cost

The cost of JEV is an estimate: the input tokens of each call times USD 0.042 per million, the price in `R/industrial_defect_classifier.R`. The client logs the tokens of each call in the TypeSafe call log, with the purpose of the call, which names the step and the configuration. The estimate does not include the output tokens. The researchers can compare the logged total with the usage that the TypeSafe account shows.

`r cost_text`

```{r}
#| label: cost-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_cost, "No JEV call has a cost in the log.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-cost
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'stringr::str_c("Calls, tokens and estimated cost of the JEV runs, by configuration. Estimated cost: input tokens times USD 0.042 per million.", cost_note)'
#| eval: !expr has_cost
#| include: !expr has_cost
cost_rows <- timing |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(n_calls)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(match(dataset, dataset_order), match(split, names(step_labels)), k)

# Table T10: one row per configuration, then the total.
t10 <- cost_rows |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset], Step = step_labels[split],
    Configuration = dplyr::if_else(split == "design", stringr::str_c("candidate ", description),
                                   stringr::str_c(description, ", k = ", k)),
    Calls = n_calls, `Input tokens` = input_tokens, `Output tokens` = output_tokens,
    `Estimated cost (USD)` = cost_usd
  ) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(tibble::tibble(
    Dataset = "Total", Step = "All", Configuration = "All configurations",
    Calls = sum(cost_rows$n_calls, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Input tokens` = sum(cost_rows$input_tokens, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Output tokens` = sum(cost_rows$output_tokens, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Estimated cost (USD)` = sum(cost_rows$cost_usd, na.rm = TRUE)
  ))
save_table(t10, "T10_jev_cost",
           stringr::str_c("Calls, tokens and estimated cost of the JEV runs.", cost_note),
           digits = 4, page_length = 25, group = "Dataset")
```

# v0.0.1 {#sec-v001}

Version v0.0.1 is the tag [`v0.0.1`](https://github.com/fmegahed/decision-models-for-industrial-image-qc/tree/v0.0.1) (commit 33ffd59). Its analysis document, tables and figures stay in the tag, and the v0.0.1 scripts in `scripts/` reproduce it. The v0.0.1 results stay in the replication record. A reader can find five weak points in v0.0.1:

1. The calibration used the validation images that chose the description. A description that separates these images well looks better on them than on new images. Thus the calibrated probabilities were too confident.
2. The label budgets were different: 103 to 104 labeled images for JEV, 100 for the CLIP baseline, and mostly different images.
3. Claude Code wrote the descriptions after it had seen test results.
4. Clef-Flash used a description that was optimized for JEV.
5. CLIP was not calibrated, and the report gave only two metrics.

| Item | v0.0.1 | This design |
|---|---|---|
| Labeled images, JEV and Clef-Flash | 3 to 4 references plus 100 validation images (pans: 4 + 16) | 50 per class for learning (the references come from it) plus 25 per class for calibration |
| Labeled images, CLIP baseline | 50 per class (pans: 10) | the same 75 per class as JEV |
| Same images for all methods | partly | yes |
| Description chosen on | the 100 validation images | the learning images that are not references (48 per class) |
| Description written by | Claude Code, which had seen test results | a fresh agent that cannot see test images or results |
| Clef-Flash description | the description of JEV | its own loop |
| Threshold | tuned on raw validation probabilities | 0.5 on calibrated probabilities |
| Calibration fitted on | the validation images that chose the description | the separate calibration set C |
| CLIP calibrated | no | yes |
| Metrics | balanced accuracy and AUC | all metrics of @sec-methods, with paired comparisons |

: What changed from v0.0.1.

The v0.0.1 runs used the test sets once, and this design keeps the same test sets. A new test set would break the comparison with the CLIP paper, and pans have no spare images. Thus the researchers know the v0.0.1 test results, but the agent that writes the descriptions does not.

# Appendix {#sec-appendix}

## Isotonic calibration {#sec-isotonic}

The plan made isotonic regression a sensitivity analysis, because Platt scaling fits 2 parameters and isotonic regression overfits with 25 images per class. @tbl-isotonic gives the test results of every configuration after both. The differences below are point differences of the test balanced accuracy, from `metrics.csv`, because `paired.csv` uses Platt only.

```{r}
#| label: isotonic-numbers
# Numbers for the text below. The point differences of P1 to P3 after Platt
# and after isotonic, with the sides of the plan (chunk paired-marks).
ba_test <- metrics |>
  dplyr::filter(split == "test", metric == "bal_accuracy", calibration != "raw") |>
  dplyr::select(model, description, k, dataset, calibration, value)
iso_diffs <- plan |>
  dplyr::mutate(k = k_main) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(ba_test, by = c("model", final = "description", "k", "dataset"),
                    relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::rename(ba_test, b_model = model, b_desc = description,
                                  b_k_side = k, b_value = value),
                    by = c("b_model", "b_desc", "dataset", "calibration"),
                    relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  dplyr::filter(is.na(b_k) | b_k_side == b_k) |>
  dplyr::transmute(comparison, model, dataset, calibration, difference = value - b_value)
iso_diff <- function(id, m, ds, cal) {
  signed(iso_diffs$difference[iso_diffs$comparison == id & iso_diffs$model == m &
                                iso_diffs$dataset == ds & iso_diffs$calibration == cal], 3)
}

# One calibration score file; with no file, an empty table with the same
# columns, so the text below shows no number and stops nothing.
read_scores_if <- function(name) {
  file <- file.path(scores_dir, name)
  if (!file.exists(file)) {
    return(tibble::tibble(actual_class = character(), prob_defective = double()))
  }
  read_csv_quiet(file)
}

# JEV with the generic description at k = 0 on pans: the scores of its
# calibration images (the 10 + 10 images of L), and the cut of each fit (the
# score where the calibrated probability reaches 0.5).
pan_k0 <- read_scores_if("jev_generic_k0_pan_images_calibration.csv")
pan_k0_y <- as.integer(pan_k0$actual_class == "defective")
pan_k0_cut <- c(platt = NA_real_, isotonic = NA_real_)
if (dplyr::n_distinct(pan_k0_y) == 2) {
  pan_k0_cut <- purrr::map_dbl(list(platt = fair$platt, isotonic = fair$isotonic), \(fit) {
    calibrate <- fit(pan_k0$prob_defective, pan_k0_y)
    stats::uniroot(\(p) calibrate(p) - 0.5, c(0.01, 0.99), tol = 1e-9)$root
  })
}
pan_k0_defective <- sort(pan_k0$prob_defective[pan_k0_y == 1])

# CLIP zero-shot with the final descriptions on textiles: its scores on C.
zero_final_c <- read_scores_if("clip_zero_final_k0_textiles_calibration.csv")

# The configurations with a negative Platt slope, and those of them whose
# isotonic fit gives 0.5 to every test image (one pooled block).
config_keys <- c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")
reversed <- slopes |>
  dplyr::filter(platt_slope < 0) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(dplyr::filter(ba_test, calibration == "isotonic"), by = config_keys)
one_block <- calibrated |>
  dplyr::filter(split == "test") |>
  dplyr::summarise(pooled = all(abs(isotonic - 0.5) < 1e-9), .by = dplyr::all_of(config_keys))
reversed <- dplyr::left_join(reversed, one_block, by = config_keys)
```

- **P1** keeps its direction for both models on every dataset, except Clef-Flash on extrusion, where `r iso_diff("P1", "clef", "extrusion", "platt")` with Platt becomes `r iso_diff("P1", "clef", "extrusion", "isotonic")` with isotonic. The JEV gap on microstructure grows from `r iso_diff("P1", "jev", "microstructure", "platt")` with Platt to `r iso_diff("P1", "jev", "microstructure", "isotonic")` with isotonic.
- **P2** mostly holds. The JEV gain on extrusion shrinks from `r iso_diff("P2", "jev", "extrusion", "platt")` to `r iso_diff("P2", "jev", "extrusion", "isotonic")`, and the small Clef-Flash gain on extrusion changes sign (`r iso_diff("P2", "clef", "extrusion", "platt")` to `r iso_diff("P2", "clef", "extrusion", "isotonic")`).
- **P3** depends on the calibration method on two datasets. *Pipe staple:* the k = 0 side of JEV has a negative Platt slope. Platt reverses its scores (balanced accuracy `r fmt(metric_value("jev", "final", 0, "pipe_staple", "bal_accuracy"), 3)`). Isotonic regression cannot, because it fits a non-decreasing function: all its probabilities pool to 0.5, so every image is called defective (`r fmt(metric_value("jev", "final", 0, "pipe_staple", "bal_accuracy", "isotonic"), 3)`). The JEV gain thus looks about twice as large: `r iso_diff("P3", "jev", "pipe_staple", "isotonic")` with isotonic against `r iso_diff("P3", "jev", "pipe_staple", "platt")` with Platt. *Pans:* the calibration images are the 10 + 10 images of L. For JEV with the generic description at k = 0, the two classes do not overlap on them: the nominal images score `r fmt(max(pan_k0$prob_defective[pan_k0_y == 0]))` or less, the defective images `r fmt(min(pan_k0_defective))` or more. Isotonic regression puts the cut inside this gap (`r fmt(pan_k0_cut[["isotonic"]])`). Platt puts it higher (`r fmt(pan_k0_cut[["platt"]])`), because `r sum(pan_k0_defective >= pan_k0_defective[2])` of the `r length(pan_k0_defective)` defective images score `r fmt(pan_k0_defective[2])` or more. On the test set, Platt thus misses many defective images (sensitivity `r fmt(metric_value("jev", "generic", 0, "pan_images", "sens"), 3)`, against `r fmt(metric_value("jev", "generic", 0, "pan_images", "sens", "isotonic"), 3)` with isotonic), and the pans gain of JEV is `r iso_diff("P3", "jev", "pan_images", "platt")` with Platt but `r iso_diff("P3", "jev", "pan_images", "isotonic")` with isotonic. Clef-Flash shows the same pattern on pans (`r iso_diff("P3", "clef", "pan_images", "platt")` against `r iso_diff("P3", "clef", "pan_images", "isotonic")`). On microstructure, the small JEV gain changes sign (`r iso_diff("P3", "jev", "microstructure", "platt")` to `r iso_diff("P3", "jev", "microstructure", "isotonic")`).
- **CLIP zero-shot with the final descriptions on textiles** (decision D89): isotonic regression works on the raw scores with no clamp. It thus separates the `r nrow(zero_final_c)` scores of C, all between `r fmt(min(zero_final_c$prob_defective), 3)` and `r fmt(max(zero_final_c$prob_defective), 3)`, and gives a balanced accuracy of `r fmt(metric_value("clip", "zero_final", 0, "textiles", "bal_accuracy", "isotonic"), 3)`. Platt gives 0.5 to every image (`r fmt(metric_value("clip", "zero_final", 0, "textiles", "bal_accuracy"), 3)`).
- **Negative Platt slopes** (decision D82): with isotonic regression, `r sum(reversed$pooled)` of the `r nrow(reversed)` configurations get one pooled block at 0.5. Every image is then called defective (the rule is 0.5 or more), and the balanced accuracy is `r knitr::combine_words(unique(fmt(reversed$value[reversed$pooled], 3)))`. The other one, Clef-Flash with the generic description at k = 2 on pipe staple, gets `r fmt(reversed$value[!reversed$pooled], 3)`: its raw scores on C are near chance (AUC `r fmt(metric_value("clef", "generic", 2, "pipe_staple", "roc_auc", "raw", "calibration"), 3)`), and isotonic regression finds several blocks.

Thus P1 and P2 do not depend on the calibration method: only differences with a Platt interval that includes 0 change sign. The size of P3 on pans and pipe staple does depend on it.

```{r}
#| label: isotonic-note
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
note(!has_decision, "Without them, the table shows the CLIP configurations.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-isotonic
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'stringr::str_c("Sensitivity analysis: test results of every configuration after Platt scaling and after isotonic regression, both fitted on C. Use the boxes above the columns to filter.", mark_caption(slope_mark(slopes$platt_slope)))'
# Readable name of a configuration.
config_label <- function(model, description, k) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    description == "baseline" ~ "CLIP baseline",
    description == "refs" ~ stringr::str_c("CLIP, same references, k = ", k),
    description == "zero" ~ "CLIP, zero-shot",
    description == "zero_final" ~ "CLIP, zero-shot, final descriptions",
    .default = stringr::str_c(model_labels[model], ", ", description,
                              " description, k = ", k)
  )
}
order_configs <- function(data) {
  dplyr::arrange(data, match(dataset, dataset_order),
                 match(model, names(model_labels)), description, k)
}

# Table A1: Platt against isotonic, every configuration.
a1 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(test_metrics("platt"), calibration = "Platt"),
  dplyr::mutate(test_metrics("isotonic"), calibration = "isotonic")
) |>
  dplyr::select(model, description, k, dataset, calibration, bal_accuracy, mcc,
                ece, mn_log_loss) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = calibration,
                     values_from = c(bal_accuracy, mcc, ece, mn_log_loss)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(slopes, by = c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")) |>
  order_configs() |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset],
    Configuration = stringr::str_c(config_label(model, description, k), slope_mark(platt_slope)),
    `BA Platt` = bal_accuracy_Platt, `BA isotonic` = bal_accuracy_isotonic,
    `MCC Platt` = mcc_Platt, `MCC isotonic` = mcc_isotonic,
    `ECE Platt` = ece_Platt, `ECE isotonic` = ece_isotonic,
    `Log loss Platt` = mn_log_loss_Platt, `Log loss isotonic` = mn_log_loss_isotonic
  )
save_table(a1, "A1_isotonic",
           stringr::str_c("Test results after Platt scaling and after isotonic regression.",
                          mark_caption(slope_mark(slopes$platt_slope))),
           digits = 3, filter = TRUE, group = "Dataset")
```

## CLIP variants

The CLIP paper rule is the raw score of the CLIP baseline at 0.5. All other rows use Platt scaling on C.

```{r}
#| label: clip-numbers
# Numbers for the text below: CLIP zero-shot with the final descriptions on
# textiles, all its scores (C and test).
zero_final_textiles <- dplyr::filter(calibrated, model == "clip", description == "zero_final",
                                     dataset == "textiles")
```

Two marks flag the rows where Platt scaling does not keep the order of the raw scores:

- † CLIP zero-shot on microstructure and on textiles has a negative Platt slope (`r fmt(slope_of("clip", "zero", 0, "microstructure"))` and `r fmt(slope_of("clip", "zero", 0, "textiles"))`; decision D82). Its raw scores run backwards (raw test AUC `r fmt(metric_value("clip", "zero", 0, "microstructure", "roc_auc", "raw"), 3)` and `r fmt(metric_value("clip", "zero", 0, "textiles", "roc_auc", "raw"), 3)`), and Platt reverses them. Its calibrated results (balanced accuracy `r fmt(metric_value("clip", "zero", 0, "microstructure", "bal_accuracy"), 3)` and `r fmt(metric_value("clip", "zero", 0, "textiles", "bal_accuracy"), 3)`) thus come from the calibration labels, not from the raw ranking.
- ‡ CLIP zero-shot with the final descriptions on textiles (decision D89) gives a probability of `r fmt(min(zero_final_textiles$prob_defective), 3)` or more to every image of C and of the test set. Platt clamps its input to 0.005 to 0.995, so all its inputs are equal, and the slope is not defined. Platt thus gives 0.5 to every image (balanced accuracy `r fmt(metric_value("clip", "zero_final", 0, "textiles", "bal_accuracy"), 3)`). The raw test AUC (`r fmt(metric_value("clip", "zero_final", 0, "textiles", "roc_auc", "raw"), 3)`) shows its ranking. The configuration stays in the results as it is, with this mark. It is not part of P1 to P3.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-clip
#| tbl-cap: !expr 'stringr::str_c("All CLIP variants on the test sets. Use the boxes above the columns to filter.", mark_caption(slope_mark(slopes$platt_slope[slopes$model == "clip"])))'
# Table A3: the CLIP rows after Platt, plus the CLIP baseline with the rule of
# the CLIP paper (raw score at 0.5), which has no Platt fit and no mark.
a3 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::filter(test_metrics("platt"), model == "clip"),
  test_metrics("raw") |>
    dplyr::filter(model == "clip", description == "baseline") |>
    dplyr::mutate(description = "paper_rule")
) |>
  dplyr::left_join(slopes, by = c("model", "description", "k", "dataset")) |>
  order_configs() |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_labels[dataset],
    Variant = dplyr::if_else(description == "paper_rule", "CLIP baseline, paper rule",
                             stringr::str_c(config_label(model, description, k),
                                            slope_mark(platt_slope))),
    dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(names(metric_labels)))
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename_with(\(x) unname(metric_labels[x]), dplyr::all_of(names(metric_labels)))
save_table(a3, "A3_clip_variants",
           stringr::str_c("All CLIP variants on the test sets.",
                          mark_caption(slope_mark(slopes$platt_slope[slopes$model == "clip"]))),
           digits = 3, filter = TRUE, group = "Dataset")

# The final JEV descriptions that the CLIP text encoder had to cut at 77
# tokens (scripts/fair_clip.R writes this file with the zero_final runs).
truncation_file <- file.path(scores_dir, "clip_truncation.csv")
has_truncation <- file.exists(truncation_file)
truncation <- if (has_truncation) read_csv_quiet(truncation_file) else NULL
```

The CLIP text encoder takes at most 77 tokens. It cut `r sum(truncation$truncated)` of the `r nrow(truncation)` texts of the final JEV descriptions (@tbl-clip-truncation).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-clip-truncation

#| eval: !expr has_truncation
#| include: !expr has_truncation
knitr::kable(truncation)
```

# Re-run steps {#sec-rerun}

These steps make all results of `results/fair/` from the images. Each step is a script in `scripts/`, run from the repository root. Steps marked **paid** call the TypeSafe API and need `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` in `.Renviron` (never commit it) and `FAIR_RECORD_ROOT`: the folder of `calls/README.md` with the budget rows (`replication_materials` in a clone of `main`). A paid JEV run does not fall back to another folder. It logs each call to `<FAIR_RECORD_ROOT>/calls/typesafe-calls.csv` and stops when `JEV_CALL_LOG` names another file. The guards of `scripts/fair_score.R` stop a JEV run that needs more calls than its budget row has left; each JEV run prints the budget file, the call log, the calls left, and the spent and maximum cost. `JEV_CHECK_ONLY=true` runs the checks only; any value other than `true` or `false` stops the run. The original runs used the calls of the "Fair comparison" row. The re-run switches log their calls with the purpose prefix `rerun` (`FAIR_PURPOSE_PREFIX=rerun`), and these calls count against a separate "Re-run" row, which must exist first.

| Step | Script | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Draw L, C, the references and the design images | `Rscript scripts/fair_draw_sets.R` | none |
| 2. Score the CLIP variants | `RETICULATE_PYTHON=<env>/python.exe Rscript scripts/fair_clip.R` | local GPU |
| 2b. Time the CLIP variants on the test images | `RETICULATE_PYTHON=<env>/python.exe Rscript scripts/fair_clip_timing.R` | local GPU |
| 3. Make the sandbox of a loop | `Rscript scripts/fair_make_sandbox.R <model> <dataset>` | none |
| 4. Run the loop | `bash scripts/fair_run_loop.sh <model> <dataset>` starts one fresh, isolated Claude Code agent in the sandbox. It reads `LOOP.md` and runs `score.sh`, which calls `scripts/fair_score.R` with `FAIR_SPLIT=design` | **paid** for JEV (up to 576 calls per dataset); local GPU for Clef-Flash |
| 5. Close the loop | `Rscript scripts/fair_close_loop.R <model> <dataset> <transcript>` | none |
| 6. Calibration and test runs | `FAIR_MODEL=<model> FAIR_DATASET=<dataset> FAIR_DESCRIPTION=<final or generic> FAIR_K=<k> FAIR_SPLIT=calibration Rscript scripts/fair_score.R`, then the same with `FAIR_SPLIT=test` | **paid** for JEV; local GPU for Clef-Flash |
| 7. Metrics, paired comparisons and k-curve | `Rscript scripts/fair_evaluate.R` | none |

: Re-run steps.

Notes on the steps:

- Step 1 rewrites `results/fair/sets/` with the same draws (the seeds are fixed). Check with `git diff` that the files do not change.
- Step 2 needs a Python 3.12 environment with torch 2.8.0 and OpenAI CLIP (`results/clip/python_environment.txt`). After the loops, `FAIR_CLIP_TEXT=final` adds the zero-shot variant with the final JEV descriptions. It skips pans and each dataset with no frozen JEV description, with a message. Run it first with `FAIR_SPLITS=calibration`, and with `FAIR_SPLITS=test` after the researchers approve the calibration results; a test run stops when the calibration file of its dataset does not exist. Run CLIP when no other process uses the GPU.
- Steps 3 to 5 run once for each model (jev, clef) and dataset (extrusion, textiles, pipe_staple, microstructure): 8 loops, each with one fresh agent. The researchers approve `LOOP.md` before step 4. Step 3 for JEV needs `FAIR_RECORD_ROOT` with the "Fair comparison" row, because `score.sh` keeps it. Step 4 runs the agent as a separate, isolated `claude -p` process with the sandbox as its working folder (@sec-loop-methods gives the command), so that it gets no project instructions, no project memory and no user settings. `--dry-run` prints the command and starts nothing. The launcher prints the path of the transcript for step 5. Step 5 refuses to overwrite a frozen description.
- Before step 6, `Rscript scripts/fair_check_call.R <model> 4` makes one call with 4 references per class (9 images), to check that the model accepts them (purpose `fair check <model> k4`). It writes only its row of the call log. `JEV_CHECK_ONLY=true` runs its checks only.
- Step 6 runs the configurations of @sec-configurations; other configurations stop. Clef-Flash needs its local server: `docker run --gpus all -p 30000:30000 lmsysorg/sglang:dev-clef sglang serve --model-path Cloudflare/clef-flash --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000`. A run of a final description stops when its loop audit flagged a tool call, unless `FAIR_AUDIT_DECISION` names the decision that accepts the flagged calls. Step 7 also writes `calibration_summary.csv` (the results on C), which needs no test file.
- Step 2b writes `results/fair/timing/clip_timing.csv` and one row per variant and dataset to `results/fair/timing/runs.csv`. It does not change the CLIP score files. It stops if `clip_timing.csv` exists.
- Each run of step 6 adds one row to `runs.csv` and an `elapsed_ms` column to its score file. JEV calls go to the TypeSafe call log, which the budget counts. Clef-Flash calls go to `results/fair/timing/clef-calls.csv`.
- `FAIR_OUT`, `FAIR_SCORES`, `FAIR_SUMMARY` and `FAIR_TIMING_DIR` send the outputs to another folder.

The chunks below run only when their switch in @sec-switches is `TRUE`. They write to `results/rerun/fair/` only, so the saved results never change:

1. The score switches (`run_clip`, `run_clef`, `run_jev`) write the new score files to `results/rerun/fair/runs/`, and their timing files to `results/rerun/fair/timing_runs/`. A re-run of a configuration passes the audit decision of its original run (`runs.csv`, column `audit_decision`) as `FAIR_AUDIT_DECISION`, when the original run has one.
2. The evaluation runs after any switch. It first fills `results/rerun/fair/scores/` with the saved score files, and puts each re-run file in place of the saved file of the same configuration and split. Thus a partial re-run (for example CLIP only) still gives a full set of scores, and no file mixes the two sources. It makes `results/rerun/fair/timing/` in the same way: the saved timing files, with the re-run rows in place of the saved rows of the same run. It then writes the summaries to `results/rerun/fair/summary/`. A re-run of a decision model must run both splits of a configuration, as `rerun_scores()` does.
3. Set `use_rerun` to `TRUE` in @sec-switches, with the switches back at `FALSE`, and render again. Every table and figure then comes from `results/rerun/fair/scores/` and `results/rerun/fair/summary/`, and the figure and table files go to `results/rerun/fair/figs/` and `results/rerun/fair/tables/`.

The same steps from the command line: run the scripts with `FAIR_OUT=results/rerun/fair/runs` and `FAIR_TIMING_DIR=results/rerun/fair/timing_runs`; make `results/rerun/fair/scores/` and `results/rerun/fair/timing/` as in item 2; run `FAIR_SCORES=results/rerun/fair/scores FAIR_SUMMARY=results/rerun/fair/summary FAIR_TIMING_DIR=results/rerun/fair/timing Rscript scripts/fair_evaluate.R`; then render with `use_rerun <- TRUE`.

```{r}
#| label: rerun-helpers
# Run one script with environment variables and arguments; the old values
# of the variables come back after the run.
run_script <- function(script, vars = character(), args = character()) {
  status <- withr::with_envvar(vars, {
    system2(file.path(R.home("bin"), "Rscript"), c(script, args))
  })
  if (!identical(status, 0L)) {
    stop(script, " failed: ", stringr::str_c(names(vars), vars, sep = "=", collapse = " "))
  }
}

# The calibration and test runs of one decision model (section Configurations):
# all calibration runs first, then the test runs.
score_plan <- tidyr::expand_grid(dataset = dataset_order,
                                 description = c("final", "generic"),
                                 k = c(0, 1, 2, 4)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(description = dplyr::if_else(dataset == "pan_images", "generic",
                                             description)) |>
  dplyr::distinct() |>
  dplyr::filter(description == "final" | k %in% c(0, 2) | dataset == "pan_images")
# The calls of a re-run have the purpose prefix "rerun" and count against
# the "Re-run" budget row (a paid JEV re-run also needs FAIR_RECORD_ROOT).
# A run of a final description stops when its loop audit flagged a tool
# call, unless FAIR_AUDIT_DECISION names the decision that accepts it. The
# re-run passes the decision of the original run of the same configuration
# (runs.csv, column audit_decision; NA when the audit flagged nothing).
rerun_scores <- function(model) {
  saved_runs <- read_csv_quiet(file.path(saved_root, "timing", "runs.csv"),
                               col_types = readr::cols(.default = "c"))
  for (split in c("calibration", "test")) {
    purrr::pwalk(score_plan, \(dataset, description, k) {
      decision <- saved_runs$audit_decision[
        saved_runs$model == model & saved_runs$dataset == dataset &
          saved_runs$description == description & saved_runs$k == as.character(k) &
          saved_runs$split == split
      ]
      decision <- dplyr::first(stats::na.omit(decision), default = NA_character_)
      vars <- c(
        FAIR_MODEL = model, FAIR_DATASET = dataset, FAIR_DESCRIPTION = description,
        FAIR_K = as.character(k), FAIR_SPLIT = split,
        FAIR_OUT = file.path(rerun_root, "runs"),
        FAIR_TIMING_DIR = file.path(rerun_root, "timing_runs"),
        FAIR_PURPOSE_PREFIX = "rerun"
      )
      if (!is.na(decision)) vars <- c(vars, FAIR_AUDIT_DECISION = decision)
      run_script("scripts/fair_score.R", vars)
    })
  }
}
```

```{r}
#| label: rerun-clip
#| eval: !expr run_clip
# Step 2: the CLIP variants, then the zero-shot variant with the final JEV
# descriptions (it skips pans and each dataset with no frozen description).
# CLIP makes no API call; the prefix keeps all re-run steps alike.
rerun_clip_vars <- c(FAIR_OUT = file.path(rerun_root, "runs"), FAIR_PURPOSE_PREFIX = "rerun")
run_script("scripts/fair_clip.R", rerun_clip_vars)
run_script("scripts/fair_clip.R", c(rerun_clip_vars, FAIR_CLIP_TEXT = "final"))
# Step 2b: the timing pass.
run_script("scripts/fair_clip_timing.R",
           c(FAIR_TIMING_DIR = file.path(rerun_root, "timing_runs")))
```

```{r}
#| label: rerun-clef
#| eval: !expr run_clef
# Step 6 for Clef-Flash (local server at localhost:30000).
rerun_scores("clef")
```

```{r}
#| label: rerun-jev
#| eval: !expr run_jev
# Step 6 for JEV (paid; needs a budget row with enough calls left).
rerun_scores("jev")
```

```{r}
#| label: rerun-evaluate
#| eval: !expr run_evaluate || run_clip || run_clef || run_jev
# Step 7. The scores of the re-run: the saved score files, each replaced by
# the re-run file of the same name (same configuration and split). The
# folder is made again at each evaluation.
rerun_scores_dir <- file.path(rerun_root, "scores")
unlink(rerun_scores_dir, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(rerun_scores_dir, recursive = TRUE)
invisible(file.copy(list.files(file.path(saved_root, "scores"), full.names = TRUE),
                    rerun_scores_dir))
invisible(file.copy(list.files(file.path(rerun_root, "runs"), full.names = TRUE),
                    rerun_scores_dir, overwrite = TRUE))

# The timing files: the saved rows of runs.csv, except the runs that the
# re-run repeated, then the re-run rows; clip_timing.csv from the re-run if
# it has one.
rerun_timing_dir <- file.path(rerun_root, "timing")
unlink(rerun_timing_dir, recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(rerun_timing_dir, recursive = TRUE)
invisible(file.copy(list.files(file.path(saved_root, "timing"), full.names = TRUE),
                    rerun_timing_dir))
new_runs_file <- file.path(rerun_root, "timing_runs", "runs.csv")
if (file.exists(new_runs_file)) {
  run_keys <- c("model", "description", "k", "dataset", "split", "candidate")
  new_runs <- read_csv_quiet(new_runs_file)
  read_csv_quiet(file.path(rerun_timing_dir, "runs.csv")) |>
    dplyr::anti_join(new_runs, by = run_keys) |>
    dplyr::bind_rows(new_runs) |>
    readr::write_csv(file.path(rerun_timing_dir, "runs.csv"))
}
invisible(file.copy(list.files(file.path(rerun_root, "timing_runs"),
                               pattern = "^clip_timing", full.names = TRUE),
                    rerun_timing_dir, overwrite = TRUE))

# The summaries of these scores.
run_script("scripts/fair_evaluate.R", c(
  FAIR_SCORES = rerun_scores_dir,
  FAIR_SUMMARY = file.path(rerun_root, "summary"),
  FAIR_TIMING_DIR = rerun_timing_dir
))
```
